questions.q: Which element has the chemical symbol O?
questions.fact: Oxygen makes up about 21 percent of the air we breathe.

questions.q: Which element has the chemical symbol Fe?
questions.fact: The symbol Fe comes from ferrum, the Latin word for iron.

questions.q: Which element has the chemical symbol Na?
questions.fact: Na comes from natrium, an old Latin name for sodium.

questions.q: Which element has the chemical symbol Ag?
questions.fact: Ag comes from argentum, the Latin word for silver.

questions.q: Which element has the chemical symbol Pb?
questions.fact: Pb comes from plumbum, the Latin word for lead, which is also where the word plumber comes from.

questions.q: Which element has the chemical symbol K?
questions.fact: Bananas are famous for having a lot of potassium.

questions.q: Which element has the chemical symbol C?
questions.fact: Carbon is in every living thing on Earth.

questions.q: Which element has the chemical symbol Cu?
questions.fact: Cu comes from cuprum, from the Latin name of the island of Cyprus, where copper was mined.

questions.q: Which element has the chemical symbol He?
questions.fact: Helium was found in the Sun's light before it was found on Earth.

questions.q: Which element has the chemical symbol Hg?
questions.fact: Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature.

questions.q: Which element has the chemical symbol Ca?
questions.fact: Calcium helps build strong bones and teeth.

questions.q: Which element has the chemical symbol Cl?
questions.fact: Chlorine is added to swimming pools to kill germs.

questions.q: Which element has the chemical symbol Sn?
questions.fact: Sn comes from stannum, the Latin word for tin.

questions.q: Which element is number 1 on the periodic table?
questions.fact: Hydrogen is the lightest and most common element in the universe.

questions.q: What is the chart that organizes all the chemical elements called?
questions.fact: The periodic table puts elements with similar properties in the same columns.

questions.q: Who created the first widely used periodic table in 1869?
questions.fact: Mendeleev left gaps for elements that had not been discovered yet, and he predicted what they would be like.

questions.q: About how many known elements are there, as of 2025?
questions.fact: As of 2025, 118 elements have been discovered or made in labs.

questions.q: What are the tiny particles with a negative charge that move around an atom's nucleus?
questions.fact: Electrons are about 1,800 times lighter than protons.

questions.q: What are the particles with a positive charge in an atom's nucleus?
questions.fact: The number of protons decides which element an atom is.

questions.q: What particles in an atom's nucleus have no electric charge?
questions.fact: Neutrons were discovered in 1932 by James Chadwick.

questions.q: What is the atomic number of an element?
choices: The number of protons in its atoms
questions.fact: Carbon has atomic number 6, so every carbon atom has 6 protons.

questions.q: What is a molecule?
choices: Two or more atoms joined together
questions.fact: A water molecule is made of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

questions.q: What do we call an atom that has gained or lost electrons?
questions.fact: Table salt is made of sodium ions and chloride ions.

questions.q: What is table salt's chemical name?
questions.fact: Sodium alone is a soft metal that reacts wildly with water, and chlorine alone is a poisonous gas.

questions.q: What is the chemical formula for carbon dioxide?
questions.fact: You breathe out carbon dioxide every time you exhale.

questions.q: What is the chemical name for baking soda?
questions.fact: Baking soda releases carbon dioxide bubbles that help cakes rise.

questions.q: What gas is made when you mix baking soda and vinegar?
questions.fact: This reaction is what makes homemade volcanoes fizz.

questions.q: Which gas makes balloons float up in the air?
questions.fact: Helium is lighter than air, so it floats the balloon up.

questions.q: Which noble gas glows red-orange in bright advertising signs?
questions.fact: Other colors in so-called neon signs usually come from different gases or coatings.

questions.q: What is the most common gas in Earth's air after nitrogen?
questions.fact: Nitrogen makes up about 78 percent of the air, and oxygen about 21 percent.

questions.q: Which liquid metal was once used in thermometers?
questions.fact: Mercury is poisonous, so most thermometers now use other liquids or electronics.

questions.q: What is rust?
choices: Iron that has reacted with oxygen and water
questions.fact: The scientific name for rust is iron oxide.

questions.q: Which metal is the best conductor of electricity?
questions.fact: Copper is used in most wires because it is almost as good and much cheaper.

questions.q: Which metal is used most in electrical wires in homes?
questions.fact: Copper bends easily and carries electricity very well.

questions.q: Which metal is light and used to make soda cans?
questions.fact: Aluminum is the most common metal in Earth's crust.

questions.q: Which element is a diamond made of?
questions.fact: Pencil lead, called graphite, is made of carbon too.

questions.q: What is pencil lead actually made of?
questions.fact: Pencils never had real lead in them, the name comes from an old mix-up.

questions.q: Which element is found in computer chips and sand?
questions.fact: Silicon Valley in California got its name from the silicon chips made there.

questions.q: What do we call a substance that speeds up a chemical reaction without being used up?
questions.fact: Enzymes in your body are catalysts that help digest food.

questions.q: What is it called when a solid turns straight into a gas without melting?
questions.fact: Dry ice does this, turning from solid carbon dioxide into a foggy gas.

questions.q: What is dry ice?
choices: Ice that has been dried in the sun
questions.fact: Dry ice is about minus 78 degrees Celsius, so you should never touch it with bare hands.

questions.q: What is it called when a gas turns into a liquid?
questions.fact: Water drops on a cold drink on a hot day come from condensation.

questions.q: What is it called when a liquid turns into a solid?
questions.fact: Water is unusual because it expands when it freezes.

questions.q: At what temperature does water boil at sea level, in Celsius?
questions.fact: High on a mountain, water boils at a lower temperature because the air pressure is lower.

questions.q: At what temperature does water boil at sea level, in Fahrenheit?
questions.fact: Water freezes at 32 degrees Fahrenheit.

questions.q: Why does ice float on water?
choices: Ice is less dense than liquid water
Ice is full of air from bubbles
Water pushes it up with magnets
Ice is lighter because it is cold
questions.fact: This is lucky for fish, because ponds freeze from the top down and the water below stays liquid.

questions.q: What is the coldest possible temperature called?
questions.fact: Absolute zero is about minus 273 degrees Celsius.

questions.q: What is the fourth state of matter, found in lightning and stars?
questions.fact: Plasma is gas that is so hot that electrons get pulled off the atoms.

questions.q: What does a pH below 7 mean?
questions.fact: Lemon juice has a pH of about 2.

questions.q: What does a pH above 7 mean?
questions.fact: Soap and baking soda are bases.

questions.q: Which acid is found in lemons and oranges?
questions.fact: Citric acid gives citrus fruits their sour taste.

questions.q: Which acid is in vinegar?
questions.fact: Vinegar is mostly water with about 5 percent acetic acid.

questions.q: What happens when an acid and a base mix?
questions.fact: Antacid tablets are bases that neutralize extra stomach acid.

questions.q: What does litmus paper do?
choices: Changes color to show if something is an acid or a base
questions.fact: Acids turn blue litmus paper red, and bases turn red litmus paper blue.

questions.q: What is a mixture where one substance dissolves completely into another called?
questions.fact: Salt water is a solution of salt dissolved in water.

questions.q: Which liquid is often called the universal solvent because it dissolves so many things?
questions.fact: Water dissolves more substances than any other common liquid.

questions.q: Why do oil and water not mix?
choices: Water molecules stick to each other but not to oil
questions.fact: Oil floats on top because it is less dense than water.

questions.q: What does density measure?
choices: How much mass is packed into a space
questions.fact: A brick and a sponge can be the same size but have very different densities.

questions.q: What are the units of temperature named after a Swedish scientist?
questions.fact: Anders Celsius created his scale in 1742.

questions.q: Which temperature scale starts at absolute zero?
questions.fact: Scientists use Kelvin because it has no negative numbers.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.fact: One newton is roughly the weight of a small apple.

questions.q: What is the unit used to measure energy?
questions.fact: A joule is named after the English scientist James Prescott Joule.

questions.q: What unit is used to measure electric power?
questions.fact: A typical LED light bulb uses about 10 watts.

questions.q: What unit measures the push of electricity, like on a battery?
questions.fact: A AA battery gives about 1.5 volts.

questions.q: What unit measures how much electric current flows?
questions.fact: The ampere is often shortened to amp.

questions.q: What does hertz measure?
choices: How many times something happens per second
questions.fact: Humans can hear sounds from about 20 to 20,000 hertz.

questions.q: What is the speed of light in empty space, roughly?
questions.fact: Light could circle Earth about seven and a half times in one second.

questions.q: About how fast does sound travel in air?
questions.fact: That is why you see lightning before you hear the thunder.

questions.q: Does sound travel faster in water or in air?
questions.fact: Sound travels about four times faster in water than in air.

questions.q: What do we call an object breaking the sound barrier, which makes a loud boom?
questions.fact: A sonic boom happens when something goes faster than sound.

questions.q: What is an echo?
choices: A sound that gets louder by itself
A sound made by animals only
questions.fact: Bats and dolphins use echoes to find things.

questions.q: What is the loudness of sound measured in?
questions.fact: Sounds above about 85 decibels for a long time can damage your hearing.

questions.q: What do we call sounds too high-pitched for humans to hear?
questions.fact: Doctors use ultrasound to see babies before they are born.

questions.q: What do we call sounds too low-pitched for humans to hear?
questions.fact: Elephants can talk to each other using infrasound over long distances.

questions.q: What happens to light when it passes through a prism?
choices: It splits into a rainbow of colors
questions.fact: Isaac Newton used prisms to show that white light is a mix of colors.

questions.q: What are the colors of the rainbow in order?
choices: Red, yellow, blue, green, orange, purple, pink
Violet, red, green, orange, yellow, blue, indigo
Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet
Blue, green, red, yellow, orange, pink, white
questions.fact: Many people remember the order with the name ROY G. BIV.

questions.q: What is the bending of light as it passes from one material into another called?
questions.fact: Refraction is why a straw in a glass of water looks broken.

questions.q: What is light bouncing off a surface called?
questions.fact: A mirror reflects almost all the light that hits it.

questions.q: Why does a red apple look red?
choices: It reflects red light and absorbs other colors
It makes its own red light
Red light is the only light in the room
questions.fact: Without light, nothing would have color at all.

questions.q: Why is the sky blue?
choices: Air scatters blue sunlight more than other colors
questions.fact: This scattering is called Rayleigh scattering.

questions.q: Why are sunsets often red and orange?
choices: The Sun cools down at night
Sunlight passes through more air, which scatters away blue light
questions.fact: At sunset, sunlight travels through much more of the atmosphere to reach your eyes.

questions.q: What type of light can give you a sunburn?
questions.fact: Sunscreen blocks most of the ultraviolet light that burns skin.

questions.q: What type of light can we feel as heat?
questions.fact: Night vision cameras and TV remotes use infrared light.

questions.q: Which type of wave do doctors use to see bones?
questions.fact: X-rays were discovered by Wilhelm Roentgen in 1895.

questions.q: How does a microwave oven heat food?
choices: Its waves make water molecules in the food jiggle
questions.fact: The microwave oven was invented after an engineer noticed a candy bar melted near radar equipment.

questions.q: What is the force that slows down two surfaces rubbing together?
questions.fact: Rubbing your hands together makes them warm because of friction.

questions.q: What is the force that slows things moving through air called?
questions.fact: A parachute works by creating lots of air resistance.

questions.q: What is the upward push that helps things float in water called?
questions.fact: A huge steel ship floats because it pushes aside a lot of water.

questions.q: Which Greek scientist is said to have shouted Eureka in his bath after an idea about floating?
questions.fact: Archimedes realized that the water rising in the tub could measure an object's volume.

questions.q: What does Newton's first law of motion say?
choices: Objects keep doing what they are doing unless a force acts on them
Every object falls at the same speed
questions.fact: This tendency to keep moving or stay still is called inertia.

questions.q: What does Newton's third law of motion say?
choices: Things fall at the same speed
Every action has an equal and opposite reaction
questions.fact: When a rocket pushes gas down, the gas pushes the rocket up.

questions.q: According to a famous story, what fell and helped Isaac Newton think about gravity?
questions.fact: Newton himself told the apple story, but it probably did not hit him on the head.

questions.q: If you drop a bowling ball and a tennis ball at the same time with no air, which lands first?
choices: They land at the same time
questions.fact: Astronaut David Scott showed this on the Moon by dropping a hammer and a feather together.

questions.q: What is the stored energy of an object high up, like a book on a shelf, called?
questions.fact: When the book falls, its potential energy turns into kinetic energy.

questions.q: What is the energy of something that is moving called?
questions.fact: The faster something moves, the more kinetic energy it has.

questions.q: What type of energy is stored in food and batteries?
questions.fact: Your body turns the chemical energy in food into movement and heat.

questions.q: What does the law of conservation of energy say?
choices: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only changed
Energy only comes from the Sun
Energy is the same as mass
questions.fact: When you switch on a lamp, electrical energy changes into light and heat.

questions.q: Which simple machine is a ramp?
questions.fact: Ramps make it easier to lift heavy things by spreading the work over a longer distance.

questions.q: Which simple machine is a seesaw?
questions.fact: A lever turns around a point called a fulcrum.

questions.q: Which simple machine is used to raise a flag up a pole?
questions.fact: A pulley uses a wheel and a rope to change the direction of a pull.

questions.q: Which simple machine is an axe blade?
questions.fact: A wedge turns a downward push into a sideways push that splits things apart.

questions.q: How many classic simple machines are there?
questions.fact: They are the lever, wheel and axle, pulley, inclined plane, wedge and screw.

questions.q: What is the flow of electric charge called?
questions.fact: Electric current in wires is made of moving electrons.

questions.q: What do we call a material that lets electricity flow through it easily?
questions.fact: Most metals are good conductors.

questions.q: What do we call a material that does not let electricity flow easily?
questions.fact: Rubber and plastic are good insulators, which is why wires are covered in them.

questions.q: What is a complete path that electricity flows around called?
questions.fact: If there is a break in the circuit, the electricity stops flowing.

questions.q: What is the kind of electricity that makes your hair stand up when you rub a balloon on it?
questions.fact: Lightning is a giant spark of static electricity.

questions.q: What do opposite magnetic poles do?
questions.fact: Two north poles or two south poles push each other away.

questions.q: What does a compass needle point toward?
questions.fact: A compass works because the needle is a tiny magnet.

questions.q: What do we call a magnet made by running electricity through a coil of wire?
questions.fact: Junkyards use giant electromagnets to lift cars, then switch them off to drop them.

questions.q: Who flew a kite in a storm to show that lightning is electricity, according to a famous story?
questions.fact: Franklin later invented the lightning rod to protect buildings.

questions.q: Which scientist discovered that moving a magnet near a wire makes electricity?
questions.fact: This idea is how power plants and generators make electricity today.

questions.q: What does a light bulb's thin wire, called a filament, do when electricity flows through it?
questions.fact: LED bulbs do not use filaments and waste much less energy as heat.

questions.q: What is Einstein's most famous equation?
questions.fact: It shows that a tiny bit of mass can turn into a huge amount of energy.

questions.q: What is the main kind of energy that nuclear power plants use?
questions.fact: Splitting heavy atoms is called nuclear fission.

questions.q: Which energy source is renewable?
questions.fact: Renewable energy comes from sources that will not run out, like sunlight and wind.

questions.q: Which fossil fuel is a black rock formed from ancient plants?
questions.fact: Coal formed from swamp plants that were buried for millions of years.

questions.q: What do we call energy that comes from the heat inside the Earth?
questions.fact: Iceland gets much of its electricity and heat from geothermal energy.

questions.q: What do we call electricity made from flowing water at dams?
questions.fact: Hydropower has long been one of the world's biggest sources of renewable electricity.

questions.q: What is a scientist who studies living things called?
questions.fact: Biology comes from Greek words meaning the study of life.

questions.q: What is a scientist who studies matter and energy called?
questions.fact: Famous physicists include Isaac Newton and Albert Einstein.

questions.q: What is a scientist who studies plants called?
questions.fact: Botanists have described hundreds of thousands of plant species.

questions.q: What is a scientist who studies animals called?
questions.fact: Zoologists may work in zoos, labs or out in the wild.

questions.q: What is a scientist who studies tiny germs like bacteria called?
questions.fact: Microbiologists help develop medicines and vaccines.

questions.q: What is a scientist who studies dinosaur fossils called?
questions.fact: Archaeologists study things made by people, not dinosaurs.

questions.q: What is the basic unit of all living things?
questions.fact: Some living things, like bacteria, are made of just one cell.

questions.q: Who first named the cell after looking at cork under a microscope in 1665?
questions.fact: Hooke thought the tiny boxes in cork looked like small rooms called cells.

questions.q: Which scientist made very strong early microscopes and first saw bacteria?
questions.fact: Leeuwenhoek called the tiny creatures he saw animalcules.

questions.q: What part of a cell holds its DNA in plants and animals?
questions.fact: The nucleus is often called the cell's control center.

questions.q: Which part of a plant cell captures sunlight to make food?
questions.fact: Chloroplasts are green because they contain chlorophyll.

questions.q: Which part of a cell is often called its powerhouse?
questions.fact: Mitochondria turn food into energy the cell can use.

questions.q: What do plant cells have that animal cells do not?
questions.fact: The stiff cell wall helps plants stand up straight.

questions.q: What does DNA stand for?
questions.fact: DNA carries the instructions for building and running a living thing.

questions.q: What shape is a DNA molecule?
questions.fact: A double helix looks like a twisted ladder.

questions.q: Which scientist's X-ray photo of DNA helped show its double helix shape?
questions.fact: Her famous image is known as Photo 51.

questions.q: Which two scientists described the double helix model of DNA in 1953?
questions.fact: Their model was built using data from Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins.

questions.q: Who is known as the father of genetics for his experiments with pea plants?
questions.fact: Mendel was a monk who grew thousands of pea plants in his garden.

questions.q: What are the sections of DNA that carry instructions for traits like eye color called?
questions.fact: Humans have about 20,000 genes.

questions.q: Who came up with the theory of evolution by natural selection?
questions.fact: Alfred Russel Wallace came up with the same idea around the same time.

questions.q: On which islands did Charles Darwin study finches and giant tortoises?
questions.fact: Darwin visited the Galapagos in 1835 on a ship called HMS Beagle.

questions.q: Which scientist created the system of giving every living thing a two-part Latin name?
questions.fact: Linnaeus published his naming system in the 1700s and named thousands of plants and animals himself.

questions.q: What is the scientific name for humans?
questions.fact: Homo sapiens means wise human in Latin.

questions.q: What are the largest groups that scientists sort living things into, like animals, plants and fungi?
questions.fact: Below kingdom come phylum, class, order, family, genus and species.

questions.q: Which kingdom do mushrooms belong to?
questions.fact: Fungi cannot make their own food from sunlight, so they are not plants.

questions.q: Which tiny living things are made of a single cell with no nucleus?
questions.fact: There are more bacteria in your body than there are people on Earth.

questions.q: Which scientist discovered penicillin, the first antibiotic, in 1928?
questions.fact: Fleming noticed mold had killed bacteria in a dish he forgot to clean.

questions.q: What do antibiotics kill?
questions.fact: Antibiotics do not work on viruses, like the ones that cause colds.

questions.q: Which scientist invented a way to heat milk to kill germs?
questions.fact: The process is called pasteurization after him.

questions.q: Who made the first vaccine, for smallpox, in 1796?
questions.fact: Jenner used material from cowpox, and the word vaccine comes from vacca, Latin for cow.

questions.q: Which disease became the first human disease to be completely wiped out by vaccines?
questions.fact: The World Health Organization declared smallpox eradicated in 1980.

questions.q: Who developed the first successful polio vaccine in the 1950s?
questions.fact: Jonas Salk chose not to patent the vaccine so it could reach more people.

questions.q: What is a virus?
choices: A tiny germ that can only multiply inside living cells
questions.fact: Viruses are much smaller than bacteria and need a microscope called an electron microscope to see.

questions.q: What do plants release into the air during photosynthesis?
questions.fact: Most of the oxygen we breathe came from plants and tiny ocean algae.

questions.q: What green substance in leaves captures sunlight?
questions.fact: In autumn, chlorophyll breaks down and the yellow and orange colors in leaves show through.

questions.q: Which part of a plant takes in water from the soil?
questions.fact: Some tree roots spread much wider than the tree's branches.

questions.q: What are the tiny holes on leaves that let gases in and out called?
questions.fact: A single leaf can have thousands of stomata.

questions.q: What is it called when water evaporates out of a plant's leaves?
questions.fact: A big tree can release hundreds of liters of water into the air on a hot day.

questions.q: What is it called when a seed starts to grow?
questions.fact: Seeds need water, air and the right temperature to germinate.

questions.q: What is it called when pollen moves from one flower to another?
questions.fact: Bees, butterflies, birds, bats and even the wind can pollinate flowers.

questions.q: What part of a flower makes pollen?
questions.fact: The pollen is made in a part at the top of the stamen called the anther.

questions.q: Which tree is the tallest kind in the world?
questions.fact: A coast redwood named Hyperion is over 115 meters tall, as of 2025 the tallest known tree.

questions.q: Which kind of tree is the largest by volume?
questions.fact: A giant sequoia named General Sherman is the largest single-stem tree on Earth by volume.

questions.q: Which plant catches and digests insects with snapping leaves?
questions.fact: The trap only snaps shut if tiny trigger hairs are touched twice quickly.

questions.q: Which fast-growing plant is actually a type of grass?
questions.fact: Some bamboo can grow almost a meter in a single day.

questions.q: What do cactuses have instead of regular leaves to save water?
questions.fact: Cactus stems are green and do the photosynthesis instead of the leaves.

questions.q: How can you tell a tree's age after it is cut down?
questions.fact: Each ring usually stands for one year of growth.

questions.q: What is the world's largest flower?
questions.fact: Rafflesia flowers can be about 1 meter wide and smell like rotting meat.

questions.q: Which plant has a tall stalk and a giant, smelly bloom and is called the corpse flower?
questions.fact: The titan arum may bloom only once every several years, and people line up to see and smell it.

questions.q: What is the name for the chain showing who eats whom in nature?
questions.fact: A food chain might go from grass to a rabbit to a fox.

questions.q: In a food chain, what are plants called because they make their own food?
questions.fact: Almost every food chain on Earth starts with energy from the Sun.

questions.q: What do we call living things like fungi and worms that break down dead plants and animals?
questions.fact: Decomposers return nutrients to the soil so new plants can grow.

questions.q: What is an ecosystem?
choices: Living things and their surroundings working together
questions.fact: A pond, a forest and a coral reef are all ecosystems.

questions.q: What is it called when two different living things help each other?
questions.fact: Bees get nectar from flowers, and flowers get their pollen spread by bees.

questions.q: What is a species that is brought to a new place and harms the plants and animals there called?
questions.fact: Cane toads were brought to Australia in 1935 and spread across much of the country.

questions.q: What is the variety of all the different living things in a place called?
questions.fact: Tropical rainforests have some of the highest biodiversity on Earth.

questions.q: What is the step-by-step way scientists test ideas called?
questions.fact: It includes asking a question, making a guess, testing it and looking at the results.

questions.q: What is a scientist's testable guess called?
questions.fact: A good hypothesis can be shown to be wrong by an experiment.

questions.q: In an experiment, what is the one thing you change on purpose called?
questions.fact: The thing you measure to see what happens is called the dependent variable.

questions.q: What tool makes tiny things look much bigger?
questions.fact: Some electron microscopes can show individual atoms.

questions.q: What tool measures temperature?
questions.fact: The first thermometers were made in the 1600s.

questions.q: What tool measures air pressure?
questions.fact: Falling air pressure on a barometer often means stormy weather is coming.

questions.q: What tool measures mass in a science lab?
questions.fact: A balance compares an object's mass with known masses.

questions.q: What glass container with straight sides and a spout is used to hold liquids in a lab?
questions.fact: Beakers have lines on the side to give a rough measurement of volume.

questions.q: What shallow round dish with a lid is used to grow bacteria in a lab?
questions.fact: It is named after German scientist Julius Petri.

questions.q: What should you wear to protect your eyes during a science experiment?
questions.fact: Even simple experiments can splash liquids into eyes.

questions.q: What is a lever's turning point called?
questions.fact: Archimedes said that with a long enough lever he could move the world.

questions.q: What is the unit used to measure frequency, like radio stations?
questions.fact: Heinrich Hertz proved radio waves exist in the 1880s.

questions.q: How many centimeters are in a meter?
questions.fact: The meter was once defined as one ten-millionth of the distance from the North Pole to the equator.

questions.q: What metric unit is used to measure the volume of a liquid?
questions.fact: One liter of water has a mass of about 1 kilogram.

questions.q: What does mass measure?
choices: How much matter is in an object
questions.fact: Your mass stays the same on the Moon, but your weight changes.

questions.q: What is the difference between mass and weight?
choices: Weight is the pull of gravity on mass
Mass changes on the Moon but weight does not
questions.fact: On the Moon you would weigh about one sixth as much but have the same mass.

questions.q: What is speed?
choices: How far something travels in a certain time
questions.fact: Speed is distance divided by time.

questions.q: What is acceleration?
choices: A change in speed or direction
questions.fact: When a car speeds up, slows down or turns, it is accelerating.

questions.q: What force pulls objects toward the center of the Earth?
questions.fact: Gravity is the weakest of nature's basic forces, but it acts over huge distances.

questions.q: Why does a feather fall more slowly than a rock on Earth?
choices: Air resistance slows the feather more
Rocks are pushed by the wind
questions.fact: In a vacuum, a feather and a rock fall at exactly the same speed.

questions.q: What is the pulling force in a stretched rope or string called?
questions.fact: Tug-of-war is a battle of tension in a rope.

questions.q: What does a lens that is thicker in the middle do to light?
questions.fact: Magnifying glasses use this kind of lens, called a convex lens.

questions.q: Why do you see lightning before you hear thunder?
choices: Your eyes are closer to the storm
Light travels much faster than sound
questions.fact: Counting the seconds between them and dividing by 3 gives the distance in kilometers.

questions.q: What causes thunder?
choices: Air heated by lightning expanding very fast
questions.fact: Lightning can heat the air to about 30,000 degrees Celsius, hotter than the Sun's surface.

questions.q: What do we call heat moving through a solid, like a metal spoon in hot soup?
questions.fact: Metals are good conductors of heat, which is why pot handles are often made of plastic or wood.
